intent: A weather quiz that beats the rainforest guess: bars put the hill village against the Amazon's city and London so the gap is absurd, a lightning flash marks the moment the monsoon hits the hills, and a pin lands on the village itself with the neighbouring town's one-year record on a card.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where is the WETTEST place on Earth?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where is the wettest place on Earth?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: India. A hill village in the north-east, where nearly 12 metres of rain fall a year.

lines.direction: ease back over the delta; three bars rise on 'Brazil' with the village off the scale as the Brazilian flag-ball thinks; an island sticker on 'Indonesia'; a rain sticker on 'quarter' as India pulses
lines.text: Brazil has the Amazon, Indonesia its islands. Even they get barely a quarter of this.

lines.direction: tighten on the Khasi Hills; a cloud sticker on 'clouds'; a white flash, the Mawsynram pin and the monsoon tag on 'hills'; a sun sticker on 'summer' as India pulses
lines.text: Monsoon clouds roll in off the Bay of Bengal, hit a wall of hills, and drop everything in summer.

lines.direction: hold on the escarpment; the 26.5 m card on 'town' with a calendar sticker; an umbrella sticker on 'shields' as the Indian flag-ball grins and India pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: The town next door once took more rain in a year than most cities see in a generation. Locals carry woven shields.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A village under a waterfall. Follow us.
